A · Finished assembly

Fig. A-1 The finished desk seen from the room. Dashed lines under the front edges: the two steel rails, hidden by the tops. Left and right are as you sit at the inside corner facing the diagonal: top A is on your right, top B on your left.
No.PartNo.Part
P01Top A, EKBACKEN 249 × 65 cm, 28 mm thickP07Rail B, steel angle 213 cm
P02Top B, EKBACKEN 249 × 65 cm, 28 mm thickP09Round adjustable foot 4 in x 8
P03ALEX 1, drawer unit 36 × 58 × 70 cmP12VIVO STAND-V300CU
P04ALEX 2, storage unit with door 36 × 58 × 70 cmP13Samsung Odyssey G5 32 in

P06Rail A, steel angle 213 cmP17HYTE Y60 on printed pedestal

What this desk is

Two IKEA kitchen tops make an L. Top A lies along the back wall and keeps the corner square; top B lies along the side wall and its end butts against top A's front edge. Each top stands 3 cm off its wall, with its square, unfinished long edge toward the wall. The far end of each top rests on an ALEX cabinet through four adjustable feet: the feet are screwed to the top, and their pads drop into printed rings on the cabinet, so the desk cannot slide on the cabinets and the two heavy boxes hold the whole frame square. Six OLOV legs stand along the two wall edges, none at the front, so the space under the inside corner is open for your knees.

That leaves the two front edges with nothing under them for more than two metres, so each one is carried by a steel angle rail screwed to the underside 12 cm back from the front edge. Under the inside corner the two rails are bolted together with two gusseted steel fittings, so the corner of top B hangs from rail A. The rails never touch a cabinet: their ends load the top, and the top loads the nearest feet. The monitor stand clamps to top A's two wall edges, 40 cm from the corner; the surface is 83.0 cm above the floor.

B · Before you begin

Read this chapter once before you pick up a drill. Budget a weekend: the steel on day one, the assembly on day two.

Safety

Fig. B-1 · The five rules that protect the tops and you.
!
NEVER A FASTENER DEEPER THAN 21 MM INTO A TOP
The EKBACKEN tops are 28 mm particleboard with a thin laminate skin. A screw or pilot that reaches the skin lifts it into a bump you will see and feel for ever. Every screw in this manual leaves at least 7 mm of wood under the laminate. 28 mm expected. If a top measures 27 mm, nothing changes: the deepest screw still stops 6 mm short of the laminate. Under 27 mm, stop and ask. If you ever substitute a screw, keep this rule. Chapter D shows every depth.
  • Laminate protection. Spread a blanket on the floor first. The tops lie face down on it, laminate on the blanket, for every marking and drilling step. Never slide or drag steel (rails, fittings, the clamp plates) across the laminate: lift it on and off.
  • Eye protection for every hole drilled in steel; drill at low speed with cutting oil. Gloves while you deburr and file the steel: drilled edges are sharp.
  • Two people to turn a top over and stand it on its legs (249 cm long). A helper is also needed to slide the finished desk off and back to the walls.

Work area

Fig. B-2 · Plan, 1:46. Footprint 252 × 317 cm; side wall 322 cm or more; 40 cm free along the open sides.

The finished desk covers 252 × 317 cm of floor in the corner: each top is 249 cm long and stands 3 cm off its wall. The room needs more than that:

  • the side wall must run at least 322 cm: in chapter G top B stands 5 cm out from its final place for a moment (far end at 319 cm);
  • 40 cm of free floor along both open sides of the desk: in chapter J the desk is pulled 40 cm into the room, away from both walls.

MEASURE ON HARDWARE Measure both walls and the baseboard thickness before you start. If the side wall is shorter than 322 cm, stop and ask before chapter G.

You also need floor for one top at a time face down on the blanket (249 × 65 cm plus room to kneel), and a bench with two clamps for drilling the two 213 cm steel rails. All steel is drilled on the bench, never under the desk.

Clear the corner before chapter F: the ALEX units are placed by the walls before the tops go on.

Printed tools (P18): print these before you mark anything

All of them are in parts/tools/; parts/README.md has print settings. Print as saved, no supports. Never scale a printed tool in the slicer: its distances are the tool. The lipped and fenced tools print lip-up and are turned over to use.

!
EVERY JIG HOLE IS BIT-SIZED
Hold the jig on, start each pilot 3–4 mm through the jig's hole, lift the jig, then finish the hole to depth with the drill guide's puck. The small centre holes are for a scriber only; nothing is drilled through them.
ToolWhat it doesQty
Edge T-square. Lip over any edge; holes named for their distance from the edge in mm: 50 (checks a ring centre 5 cm in on the ALEX), 85 (feet, 8.5 cm in, with the plate's four 1/8 in holes 46.8 mm apart round it), 100 (legs L2–L6, 10 cm in) and 150 (leg L1, 15 cm in).1
Leg jig. Lip over the wall edge; an OLOV's centre and its five 1/8 in holes in one placement: 100 pattern for L2–L6 (solid circle), 150 pattern for L1 (dashed circle, ringed holes).1
Feet corner jig. Fences on a far corner of a face-down top; a foot's centre 8.5 cm from both edges and its four 1/8 in holes 46.8 mm apart: F2, F4, F7, F8.1
ALEX corner template. A check, not the way the rings are placed (they are placed by tracing the pads, chapter G). Laid on a bare traced corner, the pencil trace must sit inside its inner engraved circle (⌀52 mm); its outer three holes are check-only. It is also the jig for the optional ALEX feet on the bottom corners (inner three 5/64 in holes, radius 14.5 mm).1
Rail marking gauge. Lip over the angle's edge; pencil notches at 19 mm (screw line on the flat leg) and 29 mm (bolt line on the vertical leg).1
Rail drill jig. Lip over the flat leg's free edge; a 1/8 in bore on the 19 line; sight grooves on the station line. PETG.1
Slot plug (fitting-centring-plug). Drops into a fitting's 21 × 12 slot; a 1/8 in bore dead centre, so the pilot cannot wander in the slot's play.2
Pilot drill guide. SET tower (45 mm for the 1/8 in bit, 35 mm for the 5/64 in) and five depth pucks: 12 PLATE, 15 LEG, 10 EDGE, 12 ALEX, 25 RAIL. Re-set the bit every time you change it.1 set
Foot height gauge. A C with 102 mm inside: all eight feet wound to the same height without a ruler.1
Wall gauge. An L: the 65 leg (6.5 cm, ALEX back to wall) and the 30 leg (3 cm, a top's raw edge to wall).1

Also print the eight locating rings (P10) now: parts/structure/foot-ring, PETG or ABS, flange down. Their 52 mm bore suits the 50 mm pad; measure your pad first (last page of this chapter).

Printed tools: how each one is used

1 · Edge T-square

Fig. B-4 · The T-square on a face-down top, lip over the edge, at its station. Hole names are mm from the edge.
  1. Turn it over so the lip hangs down. Hook the lip over the edge named in the marking table.
  2. Slide the head along the edge until the blade's centre line sits on the station you ticked with the tape.
  3. Put the scriber through the hole the table names: 50 checks a ring centre on the ALEX (5 cm in), 85 feet (8.5 cm in), 100 legs L2–L6 (10 cm in), 150 leg L1 (15 cm in). Each hole is named for its distance from the edge in mm.
  4. The four holes round 85 are 1/8 in drill holes for a feet plate (46.8 mm apart): start the four pilots through them, lift, finish with the 15 LEG puck.
  5. First-print check: hook it over a top's edge: the 100 hole must sit 10.0 cm from the edge. If not, re-print it, never scaled.

2 · Leg jig

Fig. B-5 · The leg jig hooked over the wall (unfinished) edge.
  1. Turn it over (lip down). Hook the lip over the wall edge and slide it to the leg's station.
  2. L2–L6: the 100 pattern: plain holes, solid circle, one hole toward the wall. L1: the 150 pattern: ringed holes, dashed circle.
  3. Start the five 1/8 in pilots 3–4 mm deep through the pattern's holes.
  4. The small centre hole is for a scriber only; never drill it.
  5. Lift the jig and finish each pilot with the 15 LEG puck.
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 8
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualB · Before you begin

3 · Feet corner jig

Fig. B-6 · The feet corner jig on a far corner of a face-down top, fences against both edges.
  1. Turn it over (fences down). Drop it over a far corner of the top so both fences bear on the two edges.
  2. It gives the foot centre 8.5 cm from both edges and the plate's four holes, 46.8 mm apart, square to the edges.
  3. Start the four 1/8 in pilots through it, lift it, finish with the 15 LEG puck.
  4. It does F2, F4, F7, F8. The other four feet (F1, F3, F5, F6) are 34.5 cm from the far end: the T-square's 85 pad does those, at the tape stations in chapter D.

4 · ALEX corner template

Fig. B-7 · The template on an ALEX corner, holes at 45°, 165° and 285° from the edge. Black: the outer check-only positions (radius 33 mm). White: the ALEX-foot holes (radius 14.5 mm). Dashed: the engraved ring circles; the inner one is ⌀52 mm.
  1. It checks, it does not place. Each ring is placed by tracing its pad on the cabinet top (chapter G).
  2. Check, before drilling (chapter G, step 2a): with the top lifted off, turn the template over (fences down) and lay it on the bare traced corner, fences against both edges. Your pencil trace must sit inside the inner engraved circle (⌀52 mm) all round. If it does not, re-trace.
  3. The outer three holes (radius 33 mm, engraved "outer 3 = ring check only") are check positions only: never drill through them on the top.
  4. The inner three (5/64 in, radius 14.5 mm) are drilled only for the optional ALEX feet, with the template against a cabinet's bottom corner; lift it, finish with the 12 ALEX puck. Same template for all eight corners.
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 9
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualB · Before you begin

5 · Rail marking gauge

Fig. B-8 · The angle end-on with the gauge in its two positions.
  1. Turn it over (lip down). Lay it on a face of the angle with the lip over an edge; the lip's inner face is the zero.
  2. Screw line: lip over the flat leg's free edge, pencil in the 19 mm notch, slide the full length.
  3. Bolt line: lip over the vertical leg's heel edge, pencil in the 29 mm notch, slide.
  4. Use a 0.8 mm pencil point: the notches put it on exactly 19.0 and 29.0 mm.

6 · Rail drill jig

Fig. B-9 · The rail drill jig on the flat leg (seen from above), lip under the free edge.
  1. Turn it over (lip down). Hook the lip over the flat leg's free edge.
  2. Slide it until the sight grooves on both sides sit on the station line.
  3. Hold it down and drill the 1/8 in pilot through the bore: it is on the 19 mm screw line, square, and cannot wander.
  4. Pull the jig off. Open the hole to 7/32 in without the jig; the bit follows the pilot. Nineteen holes, one jig.
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 10
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualB · Before you begin

7 · Slot plug (fitting-centring-plug)

Fig. B-10 · A fitting clamped on the rail's vertical leg, heel on its mark, plug in the first slot.
  1. Clamp the fitting to the rail with its heel on the mark from chapter E.
  2. Drop a plug into the first slot. Drill the 1/8 in pilot through its bore. Move the plug to the next slot and repeat.
  3. Take the fitting off. Open each pilot to 7/16 in; the bit follows the pilot.
  4. Why: the slots are 21 × 12 mm, so a bolt or a punch could sit anywhere along the slot. The plug fills it and puts every pilot on the slot centre.

8 · Pilot drill guide

Fig. B-11 · (a) Setting the bit in the SET tower. (b) Drilling through a puck.
  1. Set the bit: loosen the chuck, drop the bit tip-first into the SET tower's hole for it (45 mm for 1/8 in, 35 mm for 5/64 in), rest the chuck nose on the tower, tighten.
  2. Drill: stand the puck for that hole flat on the surface (or on the plate, or on the rail's flat leg), bit down its bore, drill until the chuck nose lands on the puck.
  3. Pucks: the number is the hole depth in mm. 12 PLATE (1/8 in, joining plates) · 15 LEG (1/8 in, OLOV and feet plates) · 10 EDGE (5/64 in, trim screws sideways into the raw edge, bit horizontal) · 12 ALEX (5/64 in, rings and ALEX feet) · 25 RAIL (1/8 in, through the angle, 20 mm into the wood).
  4. Re-set the bit every time you change it. A domed chuck nose: drill one test hole in scrap and measure it.
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 11
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualB · Before you begin

9 · Foot height gauge

Fig. B-12 · The C gauge on a round foot: plate face to pad bottom.
  1. Stand the foot on its pad.
  2. Slide the C over it from the side.
  3. Wind the pad until the gauge just slides on with no rock: 102.0 mm inside.
  4. All eight feet are then identical, no ruler.

10 · Wall gauge

Fig. B-13 · The two legs of the wall gauge in the gap.
  1. Hold the 65 leg (6.5 cm) between the wall and a cabinet's back while you place it, and again when you slide the desk back after the trim.
  2. Hold the 30 leg (3 cm) between the wall and a top's raw edge to check the 3 cm gap.
  3. No tape needed: it just fits, or it does not.
!
THE RULE FOR EVERY PRINTED TOOL
Every jig hole is bit-sized: start the pilot 3–4 mm through the jig, lift the jig, finish the hole to depth with the puck. Centre holes are for a scriber only. Never scale a tool in the slicer: its distances are the tool.

How sure is each number?

Every dimension in this manual carries one of three confidence labels, or a fourth label that is an instruction to you:

VERIFIEDMeasured on the purchased part, or taken from the part's own geometry file (the printed parts).
SOURCE-DEFINEDDefined by the project documents (the build manual): a design position, not a measurement. It is right by definition; you put the part there.
ASSUMPTION / FIELD CHECKAn engineering estimate or a check done on site. Confirm it before you rely on it.
MEASURE ON HARDWARENot yet measured on your parts. Measure it yourself before the step that uses it, and stop if it differs.

L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualD · Component preparation

D · Component preparation

This chapter marks both tops face down and labels the two rails. Nothing is fixed yet. Positions are in cm, as the tape reads them; thicknesses, holes and screws in mm. Every position is measured from one datum: top A's back-left corner. x runs along the back wall, y along the side wall. Top A covers x 0–249 cm, y 0–65 cm; top B covers x 0–65 cm, y 65–314 cm.

Fig. D-1 · The datum and the two tops, seen from above as installed. SOURCE-DEFINED

Which edge is which

Each top has one rounded, laminated long edge: the front. The other long edge is square and unfinished: it goes against the wall. Either short end can become the side-wall end.

Which top is A

The two tops (P01, P02) are identical. A is the one you lay along the back wall; its unfinished edge is y = 0. B lies along the side wall; its unfinished edge is x = 0 and one short end, the joint end, butts against A's front edge. Top B is top A turned 90°, never mirrored.

Fig. D-2 · Face-down convention used on every marking drawing. Stand opposite the taped reference edge (top A: at its front edge; top B: at its far end, joint end away from you): the underside is the plan mirrored left to right, so x grows to the LEFT and the datum side (x = 0) is on your RIGHT. Top B uses the same mapping.

L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 25

Never through the laminate

!
NEVER THROUGH THE LAMINATE
No screw tip and no pilot goes deeper than 21 mm into a 28 mm top: at least 7 mm of wood must remain under the laminate face. Set every pilot depth with the drill guide's puck, never by eye. 28 mm expected. If a top measures 27 mm, nothing changes: the deepest screw still stops 6 mm short of the laminate. Under 27 mm, stop and ask.
Fig. D-12 · Every fastener into the tops at its depth, 2:1, mm. The joining-plate pilot is drilled with the plate off: scribe through its holes, lift it, puck on the wood.
Fig. D-13 · Ring screws go into the ALEX top, not the desk: 15.9 mm panel VERIFIED, 2.5 mm remains.

Setting a puck

11
Loosen the chuck. Drop the bit tip-first into the SET tower's hole for that bit (45 mm for 1/8 in, 35 mm for 5/64 in), rest the chuck nose on the tower, tighten. Re-set every time you change bits.
12
Stand the puck flat on the surface (on the rail's flat leg for 25 RAIL), bit down its bore, drill until the chuck nose lands on the puck. The hole is then the depth written on the puck.

If your chuck nose is domed, drill one test hole in scrap and measure it first.

E · Steel rail fabrication and drilling

All steel work happens on the bench, before either rail goes near a top. Under the desk you only drive screws and bolts; you never drill steel there. Two identical lengths of 2 × 2 × 3/16 in hot-rolled angle arrive; either can be rail A. Tape readings in cm, caliper and drill sizes in mm.

!
MEASURE BEFORE MARKING OR DRILLING MEASURE ON HARDWARE
1 · Tape each rail from end to end and write the length on the tape label. Design length 213 cm; bought as 84 in (2133.6 mm, so about 213.4 cm). If a rail is under 213 cm, stop and check before drilling.
2 · Calipers on each angle: legs 50.8 mm, thickness 4.76 mm (the docs expect about 4.8 mm).
3 · Every station is measured from the labelled end: rail A's wall end, rail B's corner end. The far end carries any extra length. Never centre the hole pattern on the bar and never shift a hole to share out the extra.
1
Check the datum labels. The rail ends were tape-labelled in chapter D: check them (RAIL A · WALL END, RAIL B · CORNER END). Never add a second label to the other end. Measure both rails from those ends (Fig. E-1). File both cut ends of each rail smooth.
Fig. E-1 · The labelled end is 0 for every station. The last hole is at 210.5 cm on both rails, so a longer rail only lengthens the far end beyond it. SOURCE-DEFINED design length; MEASURE ON HARDWARE delivered length.
You needFor
P06 rail A, P07 rail B; one P08 fitting as the templatethe work pieces

Bits 1/8, 7/32 and 7/16 in (the 7/16 cobalt), cutting oil, flat file, 2 clamps, tape, combination square, pencildrilling and deburring; a drill press if you have one

Hook the tape over the labelled end and tick every station on the flat leg from that one hook: rail A 3.5, 28, 54, 80, 106, 132, 158, 184, 210.5 cm; rail B 2.5, 7.5, 28, 54, 80, 106, 132, 158, 184, 210.5 cm. Heel marks. On rail A, turn the vertical leg's outer face up and scribe (do not pencil) the heel positions at 51.5 cm and 52.0 cm from the wall end, squared across the leg. On rail B scribe a 0 on the vertical leg's outer face at the corner end. Scribed lines survive the paint; pencil does not.

Fig. E-5 · One hook, every station. The station line only has to cross the leg; the jig finds the 19 mm.
3
Pencil the two lines with the rail marking gauge, full length. Screw line: lip over the flat leg's free edge, pencil in the 19 notch, slide. Bolt line: gauge on the vertical leg's outer face, lip over the heel, pencil in the 29 notch, slide. The bolt line is only a check: the fitting's holes must sit on it in step 6.
Fig. E-6 · The gauge's lip is the zero; the V notches put the pencil point on 19.0 and 29.0. SOURCE-DEFINED

4
Pilot the screw holes through the drill jig. Jig lip down over the flat leg's free edge, sight grooves on the station line, hold it down and drill 1/8 in through its bore: square, on the 19 mm line, no punch needed. All 19 stations (9 on rail A, 10 on rail B). Use a drill press if you have one.
5
Open and deburr. Jig off. Open every pilot to ⌀5.56 (7/32 in) at low speed with a drop of oil on each; the bit follows the pilot. Deburr both faces with the file or a larger bit turned by hand.
Fig. E-7 · Flat leg in section. The jig's bore is 1/8 in plus a running clearance; it keeps the bit square and on the 19 mm line.
!
THE FITTING IS THE TEMPLATE VERIFIED
The fittings were measured on 23 Oct 2026: legs 100.5 × 41, two 21 × 12 slots per leg with centres 29.15 and 78.45 mm from the heel. That puts the six bolt holes at the positions below. Even so, do not lay them out with the tape: clamp the fitting on its heel mark and drill through it with the printed slot plug (steps 6 and 7), so each hole lands on its slot's centre. Check first that a plug drops into each slot without rattle. The heel of a fitting is the outside of its bend.

Clamp the fitting and pilot through the plugs. Rail with the vertical leg's outer face up. Clamp one fitting to the vertical leg with its heel exactly on the mark and its holes centred on the 29 mm line, legs the way Fig. E-8 shows. Drop a slot plug into each slot and drill the 1/8 in pilot through each plug's bore into the rail. Repeat for each of the three placements.

7
Fitting off, open to ⌀11.1 (7/16 in). Cobalt bit, slow, oil on each. The bit follows the pilot, so the hole lands on the slot's centre, not anywhere along its 21 mm. Deburr. Six holes: four in rail A, two in rail B.
Fig. E-9 · The slot plug: a stadium that fills the 21 × 12 slot with a running clearance, 1/8 in bore at its centre. Without it a punch could land anywhere along the slot.
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 34
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualE · Steel rails
!
WHY THE HOLES ON BOTH RAILS MEET WITHOUT A JIG VERIFIED
1 · The same fitting is the template for all three placements: rail A heel on the 52.0 cm mark legs toward the far end, rail A heel on the 51.5 cm mark legs toward the wall end, rail B heel flush with the corner end.
2 · The slot plug puts every pilot on a slot centre, 29.15 and 78.45 mm from wherever the heel sat. So when a fitting is bolted on, its slots sit over the holes it made.
3 · Both fittings are identical, so the inside one fits the holes the outside one made.
4 · What makes the two rails meet at the corner is rail B's end against rail A's vertical leg with B's outer face on the 52.0 cm mark. The floor test (step 8) proves it before painting: every bolt must slide in by hand. If one won't, open that rail hole with a round file now, never under the desk.
The rail drill jig is only for the 19-line screw holes, on either rail; it plays no part in the bolt holes.
Fig. E-10 · Top: the one fitting in its three placements, heel marks heavy, slots dashed. Bottom: bolted at the corner, each slot over the hole it made. VERIFIED slot centres; SOURCE-DEFINED heel marks.
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 35
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualE · Steel rails
8
Floor test. Lay both rails upside down on the floor, flat legs down, vertical legs up. Butt rail B's corner end against the outer face of rail A's vertical leg so that rail B's outer face is on rail A's 52.0 cm mark; rail B's flat leg then covers 46.9 to 52.0 cm on rail A's tape. Bolt both fittings on loosely: the outside one on the far-end side of rail B, the inside one on the wall side. Every bolt must slide in by hand. Check the corner with the combination square. If a bolt will not go in, open that hole with a round file now, not under the desk.
Fig. E-11 · Floor test, plan from above. Bolts drawn as boxes. SOURCE-DEFINED
9

Finish. Take the fittings off. Degrease both rails, scuff with 120 grit, two coats of flat black enamel, 24 h to cure. The holes need no masking.

Re-mark after painting. Put a strip of tape on rail A's vertical leg over the scribed 52.0 cm line and mark the line and 52.0 on it. Tape and re-label both reference ends again: RAIL A · WALL END, RAIL B · CORNER END. Chapter H checks rail B's outer face against this 52.0 cm mark.

The rails are now ready for the tops: rail A goes on top A with its wall end at x = 1 cm (1 cm in from the taped end), rail B on top B with its corner end projecting 12 cm past the joint end. The corner is bolted in chapter H.

Rail A. Clamp it on its line, flat leg against the top, wall end at x = 1 cm. Measure 12 cm from the front edge to the vertical leg's outer face at both ends and in the middle. Through each rail hole drill a 1/8 in pilot with the 25 RAIL puck standing on the flat leg (20 mm into the wood). Drive the two end screws first, re-check the 12 cm, then the rest: H03 #10 × 1 in Robertson on the #2 bit in the 3 in extension (the chuck would hit the vertical leg otherwise), until each head seats. Nine screws.

5

Rail B. Clamp it on its line with the corner end projecting 12 cm past top B's joint end. Pilot and screw holes 3 to 10 only, the same way: eight screws. Holes 1 and 2 go into top A in chapter H.

Fig. F-11 Plan from above. The tops are not up yet, so the cabinets are set from the walls (cm). Heavy line: the drawer fronts of ALEX 1 face you (+y); the door of ALEX 2 faces you (+x). ALEX 2 solid: where it stands now; dashed: its final place.

Stand ALEX 2 (P04) with its side 6.5 cm off the side wall and, for now, its near end 282.5 cm from the back wall, door toward you: 5 cm short of its final 277.5 cm, so that rail B's corner end comes down clear of rail A's flat leg when top B is stood on it in chapter G. It is pushed home in chapter G. Painter's tape on the floor round each one saves guessing.

!
CHECK THE ROOM
While it stands 5 cm out, top B's far end reaches 319 cm from the back wall: the side wall must run at least 322 cm. If it does not, stop and ask before chapter G.

No rings yet: they are fitted in chapter G by tracing the pads (a 50 mm pad in a 52 mm ring has only about 1 mm each side).

Optional ALEX feet (decided at the start of this chapter): fit them now, before the cabinets stand. Unscrew the stock feet, lay the unit on its back, hook the corner template over each bottom corner and use its inner three holes (r 14.5 mm). Pilot 5/64 in, 12 mm deep with the 12 ALEX puck; three #6 × 5/8 flat heads per foot down the wells, four feet per unit, all the same height.
!
MEASURE ON HARDWARE MEASURE ON HARDWARE
Before fitting ALEX feet, measure the ALEX bottom panel at an edge. 14 mm or more is fine: the 12 ALEX pilot is 12 mm deep and the #6 × 5/8 screw reaches only 9.9 mm into the panel through the foot's 6 mm roof, so 4 mm remains at 14 mm. Under 14 mm: do not fit them. The top panel measured 15.9 mm, so the bottom is likely similar and likely fine.

G · Standing the tops and fitting the rings

Two people. Both tops lie face down with their legs, feet and rails on (chapter F), every OLOV at 80.2 cm and every pad set with the foot height gauge (102 mm). ALEX 1 stands in its place; ALEX 2 stands 5 cm short of its place, its near end 282.5 cm from the back wall. Neither has rings yet: each ring is placed by tracing round its pad.

1
Stand top A on the bare ALEX 1. With a helper, turn top A over and stand it on its legs with its four pads on the bare ALEX top: lower the ALEX end first, then the leg end. Push the ALEX unit, never the top, until 3.5 cm of top shows all round the cabinet and the wall gauge's ALEX 65 leg (6.5 cm) just fits between the back wall and the ALEX.

Push the cabinet, never the top.

2
Fit the rings on ALEX 1 by tracing.
  1. With top A standing where step 1 left it, draw round each of the four pads on the ALEX top with a sharp pencil.
  2. Two people: lift top A off and lay it face down on the blanket.
  3. Check the traces before drilling anything. Lay the ALEX corner template on each bare corner, fences against the edges: the pencil trace must sit inside the template's inner engraved circle (⌀52 mm) all round. If one does not, put the top back on, push the cabinet to correct it, and trace again.
  4. Set a ring (P10) on each pencil circle, flange down. Look down through its open bottom and move it until the pencil line shows all the way round inside the ⌀52 mm bore.
  5. Hold it there. Start the three 5/64 in pilots through the ring's own holes, 3–4 mm deep, lift the ring, and finish each pilot 12 mm deep with the drill guide's 12 ALEX puck.
  6. Put the ring back and drive three H06 #6 × 5/8 in flat-head screws.
Fig. G-2 · P09 foot, P10 ring. a: a ring on its pencil circle, seen from above (1:2); b: the pad drops into the ring, section (1:2.4). Ring bore 52 mm VERIFIED (from its geometry file); pad 50 mm MEASURE ON HARDWARE. The corner-template check (item 3) is made on the bare corner, before any ring is fitted: a flat template cannot lie over a fitted ring.
3
Stand top A again and level it. Two people, ALEX end first as in step 1: the pads drop into the rings. Level along x and along y by turning the OLOV feet and the round feet until it reads flat and all four pads bear with no rock. Target: surface 83.0 cm above the floor at every corner. SOURCE-DEFINED
!
From here on, never push or lift the top alone.
If top A is not 3 cm off a wall (the wall gauge's EKB 30 leg, 3 cm), push the ALEX with the pads in the rings; the top moves with it.

83.0 cm assumes ALEX units 70.0 cm tall ASSUMPTION / FIELD CHECK until measured. With the optional ALEX feet the surface is 85.0, 87.0 or 89.0 cm (2, 4 or 6 cm feet).

Top B on the bare ALEX 2, then its rings.
  1. Wind each of top B's OLOV legs to 79.9–80.0 cm (plate face to foot), so rail B's corner end can later slide under top A.
  2. ALEX 2 stands with its near end 282.5 cm from the back wall (chapter F), 5 cm short of its place, so rail B's corner end clears rail A's flat leg. Turn top B over onto its legs with its pads on the bare ALEX 2, ALEX end first. For a moment top B's far end reaches 319 cm from the back wall: the side wall must run at least 322 cm; if it does not, stop and ask.
  3. Push ALEX 2, never the top, until 3.5 cm of top shows all round the cabinet and the wall gauge's ALEX 65 leg (6.5 cm) just fits between the side wall and the ALEX.
  4. Fit the four rings on ALEX 2 by tracing, exactly as in step 2: pencil round each pad, lift top B off, check every trace with the corner template, rings on the circles, pilots through the rings, screws.

Push ALEX 2 home; top B comes with it. Push ALEX 2 the last 5 cm toward the back wall, with the pads in its rings, until rail B's corner end touches the outer face of rail A's vertical leg and B's end meets A's front edge (y = 65 cm). Under the corner, rail B's outer face lines up with the taped 52.0 cm mark on rail A. Then wind B's legs up to 80.2 cm, until the two surfaces are flush.

H · The joint

Both tops stand on their rings (chapter G); top B's end meets top A's front edge and rail B's end touches rail A. You work from below, lying in the knee space. The two gusseted fittings bolted round rail B's end, not the joining plates, carry the inside corner of top B.

!
SEQUENCE: THE FITTINGS GO ON LAST SOURCE-DEFINED
1 · The two surfaces are flush at the joint, levelled with the feet, never packed (step 1).
2 · Rail B's end touches rail A's vertical leg; rail B's outer face is on the taped 52.0 cm mark; the L is square (step 2).
3 · Joining plates P1 and P2 are screwed across the joint (step 3). They align the tops; they do not carry the corner.
4 · Rail B's screws 1 and 2 are in top A (step 4). The inside fitting sits right under them and would block the driver.
5 · Only then the fittings (steps 5–7), and the bolts tightened last (step 8).

TIGHTENING: 25 N·m (18 ft·lb) SOURCE-DEFINED
With a torque wrench, 25 N·m (18 ft·lb), under the standard dry torque even for a grade 2 bolt. Without one, pull as hard as one hand can on a 15 cm wrench, then stop.
Why tight, not snug: this is a friction joint. The fittings' 21 × 12 mm slots leave 2.5 mm of play across and 11.5 mm along each bolt, the 7/16 in rail holes 1.6 mm, so only the clamping force keeps rail B's corner from settling.
When: only after the two surfaces are flush and rail B's end touches rail A.
Later: if the corner ever drops a millimetre, retighten these six bolts.

I · Monitor mount and accessories

The VIVO STAND-V300CU (P12) has two independent C-clamps and no base bar. Both clamp onto top A's own wall edges, never on the joint: clamp 1 centred at x = 40.0 cm on the back edge, clamp 2 centred at y = 40.0 cm on the side-wall end. The crossbar runs on the diagonal between the poles. Each lower jaw bears on a spare steel mending plate (P11), because particleboard crushes under a bare steel jaw over months. Datum: top A's back-left corner (0, 0); x along the back wall, y along the side wall.

Hang the mount

1

Lay the pad plates. Lay a spare mending plate P11 flat on the underside, on each pad outline drawn when top A was marked (chapter D), long side along the edge: x 20.0–45.4 cm, y 0.5–8.1 cm at clamp 1; y 20.0–45.4 cm, x 0.5–8.1 cm at clamp 2. Loose, no screws: the jaw holds it. SOURCE-DEFINED

!
MEASURE ON HARDWARE before hanging the clamps
Top arm reach (about 89 mm) and maximum opening (needs 31 mm or more: 28 mm top + 3 mm plate) are not measured. Open the lower clamp fully on the Option 1 holes and measure the gap with calipers; if it is under 31 mm, stop. The clamp zones are drawn 9 cm deep from the edge; if the reach measures more, keep the zone clear to the measured reach.
2

Hang both lower clamps, finger-tight only. Clamp 1 centred at x = 40.0 cm on A's back edge, clamp 2 centred at y = 40.0 cm on A's side-wall end (Fig. I-1). Use the VIVO sheet's Option 1 holes (2 and 4): top and plate together are 31 mm, under 60 mm. The clamp backs sit in the 3 cm wall gap; the lower pad lands on the plate, 13.5–63.5 mm from the edge (Fig. I-2).

3

Fit the poles and the crossbar as the spacing guide (VIVO sheet step 3). The crossbar measured 50.2 cm centre to centre, so it fixes the pole spacing. Only now tighten both clamps, with the crossbar on. VERIFIED

4

Refit the crossbar at monitor height (VIVO sheet step 6): 40–43 cm above the top (123.0–126.0 cm from the floor).

5

Hang the three screens, all landscape, and set the heights in Fig. I-3. The G5 goes on the centre bracket (VESA 75), screen centred on the diagonal at (36.5, 36.5) cm, 20 cm in front of the crossbar. The Acers go on the side arms, toed in 15°; each Acer's near end ends up about 12 cm from the G5's curved end. The side arms run along the wall behind each panel, then forward into the VESA plate.

J · Wall-gap trim (optional)

!
After chapter I.
The clamp pieces wrap round the VIVO clamp backs, so both clamps must already be fitted and tight. The trim goes on before the final push to the walls.

Parts: P19 wall-gap trim (corner, two 80 mm fillers, two clamp pieces, 240 mm segments, the short end pieces, connector tiles), H07 #4 × 1/2 in flat head × 48. Tools: tape measure, drill guide with the 10 EDGE puck, 5/64 in bit, wall gauge. No figure in this chapter uses part balloons.

1
Unload the desk. Take the screens, the PC and everything loose off the desk.
2
Measure, set, print. With the desk still against both walls, measure the gap between each top's raw back edge and the wall, in mm, at five or six points along each wall. Take the smallest reading, find it in the table, and set gap in parts/accessories/wall-gap-common.scad to the value under it. Then print the trim. MEASURE ON HARDWARE
Smallest gap (mm)27282930313233under 27 or over 33
Set gap to26272829 (as saved)303132measure again and ask before printing
WallFrom the wall corner outward: desk positions in cm, piece lengths in mmSlotted segments (cm)
backcorner (to 20), 80 mm filler (20–28), clamp piece (28–52), 8 × 240 mm, 1 × 50 mm (to 249)3rd (100–124), 8th (220–244)
sidecorner (to 20), 80 mm filler (20–28), clamp piece (28–52), 10 × 240 mm, 1 × 220 mm (to 314)3rd (100–124)

The corner piece covers each wall's first 20 cm of desk. 24 connector tiles: 11 joints on the back wall, 13 on the side wall. Cut list from parts/README.md.

L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 64
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualJ · Wall-gap trim
3
Pull the desk out, 40 cm from both walls. Two people, one at each ALEX unit: slide the whole desk away from both walls. The ALEX units slide on their feet and the pads stay in their rings. Nothing comes apart.
Fig. J-1 · Plan, seen from above: x grows to the right, y toward you, back wall at the top (1:40). Dashed: the desk in place, 3 cm off both walls. Grey: pulled 40 cm off both, so the raw back edges are open to work on.
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 65
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualJ · Wall-gap trim
4
Build each chain from the corner outward. Corner piece, 80 mm filler, clamp piece with its notch round the clamp back, then the 240 mm segments (slotted ones where the cut list says), ending with the short piece. Butt every joint and push a connector tile up into the pockets.
Fig. J-2 · Chain order along both walls, straightened out: the wall corner on the left, desk positions in cm growing to the right, piece lengths in mm (1:20). The notch (white, in K) wraps the clamp back, 80 mm long and 17.5 mm proud VERIFIED.
Fig. J-3 · Connector tile (1.8:1, mm), one under every joint, pins up. It bridges the 20 × 12 mm pockets of two butted pieces.

Every piece, the corner included, has a pocket on its underside at each end, over the gap. Butt two pieces, then push a tile up into both pockets until its pins seat: the joint cannot step, bow or drift, and nothing shows on top.

If a wall is out and the notch misses the clamp, change the 80 mm filler's seg and reprint it, nothing else.

L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 66
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualJ · Wall-gap trim
5
Pilot and screw. Through each lip hole, pilot 5/64 in, 10 mm deep, drill horizontal, with the drill guide's 10 EDGE puck held against the raw edge. Drive an H07 #4 × 1/2 in flat head into each: two per segment, one per corner leg, one each side of a clamp notch.
Fig. J-4 · Trim on the raw back edge, section across the edge (1.8:1, mm), seen from the side-wall end looking along the back wall (x grows away from you): the wall on the left, the desk on the right. 12 mm rests on the surface, the 20 mm lip drops into the gap, the screw sits 14 mm below the surface: nothing shows on top and nothing goes into the top face. Profile from parts/accessories/wall-gap-common.scad SOURCE-DEFINED; top 28 mm thick MEASURE ON HARDWARE.
6
Slide the desk back. Two people again, one at each ALEX, until the wall gauge's ALEX 65 leg (6.5 cm) just fits between the wall and each ALEX. The trim's outer edge stops 1 mm short of the wall.
7
Load the desk again. Put the screens, the PC and everything else back in their chapter I positions: chapter K checks the desk with everything in place.

Retighten every screw after two weeks.

K · Final inspection and load testing

Ten checks, in order, before you call the desk done. Each is an ACCEPTANCE CHECK: a pass or fail you can see or measure. Several of them test a STRUCTURAL ESTIMATE from the design review that has not been measured on this desk; the check says which. Write the results in the boxes and in the sign-off table at the end of this chapter. Datum for every drawing: top A's back-left corner (0, 0).

Check 1 · Surface height at the six corners ACCEPTANCE CHECK

1

Measure from the floor to the top face at the six supported corners 1 to 6, then the inside corner 7 last (Fig. K-1). Every reading 83.0 cm ± 0.3 cm (82.7 to 83.3 cm). With the optional ALEX feet fitted, read instead: 2 cm feet 85.0 cm, 4 cm feet 87.0 cm, 6 cm feet 89.0 cm, each ± 0.3 cm. If a corner is out, adjust only what carries it, then measure all seven again (positions x, y in cm): corner 1 (0, 0) by legs L1 and L2; corners 2 (249, 0) and 3 (249, 65) by the ALEX 1 feet; corners 4 (65, 314) and 5 (0, 314) by the ALEX 2 feet; corner 6 (0, 65) by leg L4. Corner 7, the inside corner (65, 65), has no support of its own: it follows the joint, so it is measured last and set by chapter H, never adjusted here.

Fig. K-1a Corners 1–6, and the inside corner 7 measured last.
Fig. K-1b Tape from the floor to the top face, at the corner.

Check 2 · Level and flush across the joint ACCEPTANCE CHECK

2

A level across the joint reads flat both ways: across it (1) and along it (2). A fingertip drawn across the joint (3) finds no step. Level the two tops with the OLOV feet and the round feet, never by packing anything under the joining plates.

Fig. K-2 Plan of the joint at y = 65 cm. 1, 2: level positions; 3: fingertip; 4: where the straightedge of check 5 goes, at the inside corner.

Check 3 · Corner load test ACCEPTANCE CHECK

!
NEVER STAND OR SIT ON THE DESK
The test load is a known weight: 20 kg of water and books. Do not stand or sit on the corner; that is not what the beam was sized for.
Fig. K-3a Plan. Case faces 10 cm in from top B's front edge and from the joint (case size schematic). R: reading point.
3

Rest a straightedge from leg L1's line across the corner. With no weight on, the gap at the corner (R) must read 0.

Set 20 kg (a case of water plus a few books) on top B's inside corner, 10 cm in from both edges, then read the gap at R again: no more than 2 mm. The estimate is about 1 mm. STRUCTURAL ESTIMATE

Lift the weight off. The corner returns to where it was, nothing creaks, no screw or bolt has moved.

Tests: sag at the inside corner (rail A carrying rail B's corner reaction) and corner-joint slip (the six fitting bolts holding by friction). STRUCTURAL ESTIMATE

Gap, no weight (0)Gap with 20 kg (mm)Returned?Creak / moved?
Fig. K-3b Elevation along the straightedge, from leg L1 to the corner. The case stands beside the straightedge, not under it.

Check 4 · All eight pads bear ACCEPTANCE CHECK

4

At each of the eight feet F1–F8, rock the pad sideways in its ring by hand. Do not turn it: turning changes its height. None rocks or lifts. A pad that rocks or lifts is not bearing: see chapter L, "Top moves on its ALEX".

Tests: the racking estimate (eight pads captive in their rings hold the frame against a sideways push) and the ALEX load share. STRUCTURAL ESTIMATE

Fig. K-4 Foot P09 on its pad in ring P10 on the ALEX top.

Check 5 · Straightedge at the joint, now and later ACCEPTANCE CHECK

5

Lay a straightedge across the joint at the inside corner (Fig. K-2, position 4) and write down any step. Check it again after two weeks and after the first month. If today's step is bigger than Day 0's, retighten the six fitting bolts (25 N·m, chapter L).

Fig. K-5 Section across the joint at the inside corner. Step drawn exaggerated.

Check 6 · Sideways push ACCEPTANCE CHECK

6

Push the desk sideways along each wall. No sway at the top beyond a few millimetres, and no top moves on its ALEX.

Tests: racking. The OLOV legs give almost no racking resistance; the two ALEX units, locked to the tops by the pads in their rings, do. STRUCTURAL ESTIMATE

Fig. K-6 Push along the back wall, then along the side wall.

Check 7 · Screw tips ACCEPTANCE CHECK

7

No screw tip visible, or felt as a bump, on either laminate face. Run a hand over both tops, above every leg, foot plate, rail screw and joining plate.

Check 8 · Knees clear ACCEPTANCE CHECK

8

Knees clear. Sit at the corner and slide in: nothing within reach of a knee or thigh. The rails' lower edge is 75.1 cm from the floor, 12 cm back from the front edge.

Fig. K-7 Section through top A's front at rail A.

Check 9 · ALEX fronts ACCEPTANCE CHECK

9

Both ALEX fronts open fully (ALEX 1's drawers, ALEX 2's door) without touching a foot or a leg.

Check 10 · Retighten ACCEPTANCE CHECK

10

Retighten every screw after two weeks, then repeat check 5.

L · Maintenance and troubleshooting

Schedule

WhenDoSee
Day 0Write down the step at the joint (straightedge at the inside corner).Chapter K, check 5, Fig. K-5
Two weeksRetighten every screw. Straightedge at the joint again; if today's step is bigger than Day 0's, retighten the six fitting bolts to 25 N·m. Look at each printed ring and its three screws.Chapter K, checks 5 and 10; troubleshooting
One monthStraightedge at the joint again; if today's step is bigger than Day 0's, retighten the six fitting bolts.Chapter K, check 5
Any timeIf the corner ever drops a millimetre, retighten the six fitting bolts.Corner bolts, below
!
NEVER DEEPER THAN 21 MM INTO A TOP
The tops are 28 mm particleboard with a thin laminate skin; a screw reaching the skin lifts it. Replace a screw only with the same size. If a top measures 27 mm, nothing changes: the deepest screw (rail #10 × 1 in) still stops 6 mm short of the laminate. Under 27 mm, stop and ask. SOURCE-DEFINED

Corner bolts

Boltssix 3/8-16 × 1-1/2 in hex bolts, grade 5 (H08), washer under head and nut (H09), nylon-insert nuts (H10): four through rail A's vertical leg, two through rail B's leg with a fitting on each side Torque25 N·m (18 ft·lb); without a torque wrench, pull as hard as one hand can on a 15 cm wrench, then stop Whya friction joint: only the clamping force keeps rail B's corner from settling. Each fitting leg has two 21 × 12 mm slots, centred 29.15 mm and 78.45 mm from the heel, which leave each bolt 2.5 mm of play across and 11.5 mm along; the rails' 7/16 in holes leave 1.6 mm. VERIFIED Ordertighten only with the two surfaces flush and rail B's end touching rail A

The mending plates across the joint align the tops; they do not carry the corner. SOURCE-DEFINED

L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 74
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualL · Troubleshooting

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Corner has dropped; step at the joint grewThe six fitting bolts lost clamping force (friction joint); supports settlingBring the surfaces flush with the OLOV feet and the round feet, never by packing anything under the joining plates. Check rail B's end still touches rail A. Retighten all six bolts to 25 N·m. Write the new step down (Fig. K-5).
Top moves on its ALEX, or a pad rocks or liftsA pad is out of its ring or not bearingLift that ALEX end a few millimetres and slide the ALEX unit, never the top alone, until the pads drop into their rings (chapter G). Wind the pads until a level reads flat along x and y and all pads bear; never unscrew a plate; re-check 83.0 cm at the corners (chapter K, Figs. K-1 and K-4).
Printed ring cracked or its screws looseRing wall overloaded by a sideways pushInspect at two weeks. A crack: reprint the ring (parts/structure/foot-ring.stl), PETG or ABS, flange-down: 52 mm bore, 3 mm wall, 75 × 2.5 mm flange. Refit with #6 × 5/8 in flat-head screws (H06), 5/64 in pilots 12 mm deep (12 ALEX puck). Never run the desk with a ring missing.
Leg moves or wobblesOLOV plate screws looseRetighten the five M4 × 16 mm screws (H01). A screw that spins: repair the hole (below), re-pilot 1/8 in, 15 mm deep (15 LEG puck). Re-set the OLOV to 80.2 cm, or the ALEX-feet table's number (chapter F).
Monitor clamp creepsClamp loosened over timeRetighten the clamp with the crossbar fitted. Keep the steel plate (P11) flat on its outline under the jaw. Never add a soft pad under the jaw.
Screw spins (stripped)Hole worn in the particleboardBack it out, fill the hole with wood glue and a couple of matchsticks, let it dry, re-pilot.
A mark is off by more than 2 mmMarking errorRedraw it. A stray 1/8 in hole in the underside does no harm.
A fitting bolt will not go inHoles not quite in lineWith the bolts out and the fittings off, open the hole in the rail with a round file, never under the desk; never force a bolt.
Fig. L-1 A screw that spins: back it out, fill the hole with wood glue and a couple of matchsticks, let it dry, re-pilot with the step's own bit and depth.

Every fix above is from the build manual and the build guide SOURCE-DEFINED.
